findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this bucket - including the uploaded vendor roster spreadsheet - are stored without an enforced default SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 policy.

The bucket sets no ACL and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy in the configuration, so the access posture is undefined and public ACLs or policies could expose the vendor data with no account-level guardrail declared here.
No logging block is configured, so requests against this bucket are not recorded, hindering detection and forensic reconstruction of unauthorised data access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects can be silently overwritten or permanently deleted by an attacker with write access with no recoverable prior version.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this financial data bucket, so unauthorised reads or exfiltration of ledger exports would leave no audit trail.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true, allowing destructive overwrite or deletion of financial records without any recovery path.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without an enforced default encryption policy, unlike the audit_trail bucket which uses SSE-KMS.
The runbooks bucket defines no default server-side encryption; operational runbooks commonly contain sensitive internal procedures and credential-adjacent detail stored unencrypted by default.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbook content is not recorded for audit or incident response.

findings.issue_category: invalid canned ACL on log bucket
findings.description: The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL (an apparent corruption of "log-delivery-write"), so the intended restrictive log-delivery grant is not applied to the audit log destination bucket and its access control state is not what the author intended.

force_destroy = true on the central audit/log bucket allows all audit evidence to be deleted together with the bucket, and no object lock or MFA delete protects log integrity, undermining non-repudiation of security logs.

The vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/business data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which itself has no default encryption, so the object rests without enforced encryption.

Like the other buckets in this file, the model artifacts bucket relies solely on a private canned ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy, so a later ACL or policy change could expose artifacts publicly with no account-level guardrail.
The audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so the log-delivery-oriented ACL grants are the only control preventing public or cross-account exposure of security logs.
